feed.title: The Elon Gazette
feed.subtitle: Weekday briefing on what Elon Musk is saying and doing
feed.rights: The Elon Gazette is compiled from public posts on X and published reporting. Quotes are reproduced verbatim unless marked as translated or paraphrased.

entry.title: Friday, October 9, 2026: A spectrum "earthquake," a medal for a "modern-day Edison," and a bot for hire
entry.summary:
Since late Thursday morning EDT, Elon Musk posted about 50 times, and two events set the tone. At the White House "Science: A New Golden Age" summit, President Donald Trump hung the National Medal of Science on him, calling him "an industrial titan, a brilliant engineer, and one of the greatest technology founders ever to live." A few hours later SpaceX announced a deal to buy a nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management. Musk called it "the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle" for complete phone coverage in America, and by Friday morning U.S. and European telecom stocks were sliding.

Between those stories, Musk kept pitching Grok Bot as cheap, capable labor ("like hiring a super smart, hard-working person for peanuts"). He said bots will manage Grokipedia and pointed to a legal benchmark where Grok 4.7 ranked first. He also joked that AI labs should test on Delta flights, backed Anthropic's new rule against abusing Claude, reacted to three OpenAI safety researchers going public about their firings, and agreed with a fan that Tesla's new European name for its driver-assist software undersells it.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Starlink's India fight, a Grok Bot shopping clerk, and a White House medal
entry.summary:
In the day and a half since Wednesday morning EDT, Elon Musk posted about 93 times. The through-line was Starlink: he accused Indian "oligarchs" of blocking a license after five years of compliance, asked whether Mukesh Ambani is "the real boss of India," celebrated Starlink Mobile in Bangladesh, cheered Koninklijke Luchtvaart Maatschappij (KLM) picking Starlink for free intercontinental Wi-Fi, and welcomed Crew-12's Dragon splashdown off Los Angeles. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) clearance for 15,000 next-generation direct-to-phone satellites sat under it all.

On the product side, Grok Bot gained a Shopify connector, a promise that simple requests will ride a fast Grok 4.8, and an open router that can call Claude Opus 5.5 and other models. This afternoon, President Donald Trump is set to award Musk the National Medal of Science at the White House "Science: A New Golden Age" summit alongside Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang, and Lisa Su.
